desc: The Institute of Field Physics received its certificate of incorporation on 7 September 1955 and was placed inside the physics department at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, directed by Bryce and Cecile DeWitt and funded principally by the Winston-Salem industrialist Agnew Bahnson. Its inaugural event was the Conference on the Role of Gravitation in Physics at Chapel Hill in January 1957, now known as GR1. It sits on the same money as the board's existing Martin thread: George Trimble and the Glenn L. Martin Company bought a Founder's Membership for $5,000 while the company was separately standing up RIAS, whose first researcher was Louis Witten. The thing a node must carry is what the Institute wrote about itself. On John Wheeler's insistence a 'Protection Clause' was attached to every IOFP publicity statement declaring that the work 'has no connection with so-called "anti-gravity research" of whatever kind and for whatever purposes', and the department's own history says the instruction to avoid anti-gravity connotations runs through the founding correspondence like a mantra.

dossier.narrative: Two records opened in this corpus refine the node rather than extend it, and both refinements cut against an easy reading. The first is sponsorship. The conference report's title page reads that the meeting was held under the sponsorship of the International Union of Pure and Applied Physics, with financial support from UNESCO, the National Science Foundation, the Wright Air Development Center of the US Air Force, and the Office of Ordnance Research of the US Army. IUPAP sponsored it; four bodies paid for it; and the Foreword says the report exists because it was a necessary requirement to obtain conference funds. The Air Force's imprint is on the cover because the report was the condition of the money, not because the Air Force convened the meeting. The second is naming and dating. The conference title page says the Institute was established in 1956 in the Department of Physics, while the certificate of incorporation is dated 7 September 1955: two different acts, which a node should not collapse. And Talbert's Herald Tribune series of 20 November 1955 shows the press knew it at its founding as the Institute of Pure Physics, approved by the trustees that month with Gordon Gray's approval. Four of the forty-six conference participants were serving in US military research offices, which is the fact worth carrying: not that the Air Force ran it, but that it was in the room.
openQuestions: What the change of name from Institute of Pure Physics to Institute of Field Physics turned on, which no opened record states.
Whether the Wright Air Development Center's financial support carried any condition beyond the report.
dossier.whatItIs: A privately endowed gravitation-research institute placed inside the physics department at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, incorporated 7 September 1955, directed by Bryce and Cecile DeWitt and funded principally by the Winston-Salem industrialist Agnew Bahnson. Its inaugural event was the January 1957 Conference on the Role of Gravitation in Physics, now known as GR1.
dossier.whyImplicated: It is where the aerospace money and the academic gravity work meet on the same page: George Trimble and the Glenn L. Martin Company bought a Founder's Membership for $5,000 while the company was separately standing up RIAS, whose first researcher was Louis Witten. And it is the body that wrote its own anti-gravity disclaimer into every publicity statement, which is a documented instance of an institution managing the reputational risk this board maps.
